rv.q: If you're in shouting distance of Aurora, you won't regret the roughly 50 bucks or the two hours in its company.
Directed with a firm hand and a restrained ferocity by Jim Corti, Paramount's gifted Artistic Director, Shepard's play bursts onto the intimate Copley Theatre stage like an explosion.
Ball and Page's acting is superb. Their performances are multilayered. The tension between them is evident the moment the lights go down.
I will tell you that you will laugh, you will think and you will love this production.

Lee swears he’s not there to mess anything up as Austin is housesitting for their mother. Austin even warns him not to draw too much attention to himself, but Lee still comes back with a stolen TV. Lee plays games with Austin’s agent much to Austin’s dismay, turning into a charming and affable dealmaker on the golf course.
If you like Shepard's work, or mid-century contemporary plays, this could be a great production for you.
